title: Faith
definition: Faith is trusting in God and receiving Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord according to the promises of the Gospel.
summary: Faith receives Christ and rests in Him rather than in human works or self-righteousness.
christFocus: Jesus is the object of saving faith, the faithful Savior who is worthy to be trusted completely.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Faith is more than awareness of facts. Saving faith includes trust in Christ and reliance upon Him. It receives the Gospel promise and rests in the person and work of Jesus.

Faith does not save because it is strong in itself. Faith saves because it unites the believer to Christ, who is strong, sufficient, and faithful. The weakest true faith has a strong Savior.

Faith also continues in the Christian life. Believers walk by faith, pray by faith, endure by faith, and obey by faith because they trust the God who has spoken.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some people place confidence in religious activity, emotional experiences, or personal morality. Faith matters because it directs the heart away from self and toward Christ as the only sufficient Savior.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Christ rather than the strength of your faith. Feed faith through Scripture, prayer, and obedience. When doubts come, bring them honestly to the Lord and keep trusting His promises.
